history.summary: A small 1882 shrine in Shivaji Peth famous for its pillarless architecture - 'Binkhambi' means 'without pillars'. The black-stone Ganesha idol (with shendur applied) was discovered while desilting/repairing a well at the site, and the sanctum was built exactly over the find spot; the idol is believed older than the temple. The inner temple and its 25'x25' mandap carry the stone-masonry dome on arches that transfer the load to the four walls, with no pillars or columns anywhere - a construction that draws architecture and archaeology students from across India. Exterior carved stone tortoise among other carvings. Formerly managed by the Josirao family, hence 'Joshirao Ganapati'.

name: Binkhambi Ganesh Mandir
town_description: A small but popular shrine on Mahadwar Road (Savarkar Marg) in Shivaji Peth, ~2.5 km from Kolhapur Railway Station and a short walk from the Mahalakshmi (Ambabai) Temple, set in the middle of a busy market with shops and eateries.

travel.airport: Kolhapur Airport (Chhatrapati Rajaram Maharaj Airport), ~10 km
travel.railway: Kolhapur Railway Station (Chhatrapati Shahu Maharaj Terminus), ~2.5 km
travel.road: Mahadwar Road / Savarkar Marg, Shivaji Peth; auto and taxi easily available; entry free

visitor_information.best_time: November to February (winter); morning and evening visits avoid crowds
visitor_information.opening_hours: 5:30 AM to 8:00 PM daily (entry free); busiest during Ganesh Chaturthi
